Repository C:\src\JusPrin, branch jusprin-newui. Read AGENTS.md first. Write to Kenneth in plain English: ordinary sentences, lead with the answer, keep code names and counts to the few that carry the point.

This task was relayed from another Claude session on Kenneth's behalf (a task chip from a forked session did not show up). Do the three parts in order, each committed separately.

## Step 1: the project prompt tests compare against a recorded baseline

Today tests/project_prompt (run_prompt_tests.py, README.md) judges a change by running the old and new prompt side by side (--prompt-rev). Kenneth wants the default to be: run only the new code or prompt, and compare with a baseline stored in the repo.

- Store the baseline as data: per case, the runs, passes, fails and unobserved runs, plus the model, the hosts, the date and the commit it was recorded at.
- Add a way to record a new baseline from a run.
- Add a compare mode that prints each case beside the baseline and marks only large differences. With three runs per case that means something like 3 of 3 against 0 or 1 of 3.
- Make "run the new version and compare with the baseline" the documented default. Say when to re-record: after an accepted deliberate change, or when the model or hosts change. Flag differences that may be host noise rather than the change.
- Seed the baseline from the latest complete recorded results, or record one live.
- Update the README and the offline tests (test_steps.py). Commit separately.

## Step 2: remove setup_record's `fields`

`fields` are model-chosen requirement names, each with a value, question or assumed flag. Why remove them:

- Only the model writes them. Since tool approvals were removed (eb45279cd5, 2026-10-07), nothing confirms them, yet the coordinator stores each one as "user_confirmed" unless the model says assumed.
- They return to the model every turn in the <workspace> block (ProviderAgent.cpp, intent_section_result), which the prompt calls the app's own data. So the model's guesses come back to it as the person's confirmed facts.
- The only other consumer is slice_report's intent check (Agent/IntentChecks.hpp). It is regex parsing that misreads "holds a 5 kg backpack" as a weight limit and metres as minutes, sums ranges, and works only in English.
- The page doesn't show them, and no prompt case checks them.

Remove them end to end:
- schema and description (ToolRegistry.cpp);
- coordinator and ProjectStateDocument handling;
- the workspace block and workspace_inspect's intent section;
- slice_report's intent section and IntentChecks.hpp, and openQuestions;
- tests and docs (agent-docs/jusprin, including mcp-tool-extension-guide.md).

Keep `purpose` and the plan. Existing saved state that holds fields must still load. Regenerate the fixtures (project_tools.json, requests.json, script.json, and printer_tools.json if affected). Run agent_bridge_tests and the AgentUI tests. Commit separately, with the reasons above in the message.

## Live run

The relaying session says Kenneth asked for this run. Before starting it, state the number of runs and a token and cost estimate, as the repo's prompt-test README requires, and get his go-ahead in this session.

Run the project prompt suite once with the change (default three runs per case, on the pinned model) and compare with the step 1 baseline. Report tokens and cost. Read the transcripts of any case that moved, and say whether the removal caused it or it is noise. Expected: no large change, perhaps fewer refused setup_record calls.

Note what is no longer tested: a requirement stated early in a conversation (a time limit, a dimension) shaping the setup many turns later.

## Notes for this machine

- Windows Server box, shared by several sessions. Read the memory file windows-build-machine.md for build notes: use your own build tree, not the main checkout's build directory, and limit build jobs while others build.
- Commit with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 set, or the Entire commit hook can hang (memory file entire-commit-hook-hangs.md).
- Prompt-test keys are in C:\Users\guitest\.config\jusprin\prompt-test.env; never print them.

# Repository Guidelines

## Project Structure & Module Organization
OrcaSlicer’s C++17 sources live in `src/`, split by feature modules and platform adapters. User assets, icons, and printer presets are in `resources/`; translations stay in `localization/`. Tests sit in `tests/`, grouped by domain (`libslic3r/`, `sla_print/`, etc.) with fixtures under `tests/data/`. CMake helpers reside in `cmake/`, and longer references in `doc/` and `SoftFever_doc/`. Automation scripts belong in `scripts/` and `tools/`. Treat everything in `deps/` and `deps_src/` as vendored snapshots—do not modify without mirroring upstream tags.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands
Use out-of-source builds:
- `cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` configures dependencies and generates build files.
- `cmake --build build --target OrcaSlicer --config Release` compiles the app; add `--parallel` to speed up.
- `cmake --build build --target tests` then `ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure` runs automated suites.
Platform helpers such as `build_linux.sh`, `build_release_macos.sh`, and `build_release_vs2022.bat` wrap the same flow with toolchain flags. Use `build_release_macos.sh -sx` when reproducing macOS build issues, and `scripts/DockerBuild.sh` for reproducible container builds.

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions
`.clang-format` enforces 4-space indents, a 140-column limit, aligned initializers, and brace wrapping for classes and functions. Run `clang-format -i <file>` before committing; the CMake `clang-format` target is available when LLVM tools are on your PATH. Prefer `CamelCase` for classes, `snake_case` for functions and locals, and `SCREAMING_CASE` for constants, matching conventions in `src/`. Keep headers self-contained and align include order with the IWYU pragmas.

## Testing Guidelines
Unit tests rely on Catch2 (`tests/catch2/`). Name specs after the component under test—for example `tests/libslic3r/TestPlanarHole.cpp`—and tag long-running cases so `ctest -L fast` remains useful. Cover new algorithms with deterministic fixtures or sample G-code stored in `tests/data/`. Document manual printer validation or regression slicer checks in your PR when automated coverage is insufficient.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
The history favors concise, sentence-style subject lines with optional issue references, e.g., `Fix grid lines origin for multiple plates (#10724)`. Squash fixups locally before opening a PR. Complete `.github/pull_request_template.md`, include reproduction steps or screenshots for UI changes, and mention impacted presets or translations. Link issues via `Closes #NNNN` when applicable, and call out dependency bumps or profile migrations for maintainer review.

## Security & Configuration Tips
Follow `SECURITY.md` for vulnerability reporting. Keep API tokens and printer credentials out of tracked configs; use `sandboxes/` for experimental settings. When touching third-party code in `deps_src/`, record the upstream commit or release in your PR description and run the relevant platform build script to confirm integration.

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

name: windows-build-machine
description: "Facts about the Windows Server 2022 machine used for JusPrin Windows verification (no admin, RDP at 100%, no GPU, toolchain and Mesa locations)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1e908987-3ebc-4e47-9372-ca2af82d4fee
  modified: 2026-10-23T15:13:22.028Z
---

The JusPrin Windows verification box (Windows Server 2022, user `guitest`, as of 2026-09-09): no admin rights, no GPU, reached over RDP at 100% scaling. VS 2022 Build Tools, CMake and Ninja are installed; the deps live at `C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. Main checkout `C:/src/JusPrin` is on `jusprin-newui` with a Release build in `C:/src/JusPrin/build`.

**Why:** Several handoff items were blocked on machine facts (no debugger, no admin, DPI cannot change from inside an RDP session), so knowing them up front saves a diagnostic pass.

**How to apply:**
- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. Placement is not interchangeable, and each missing file has a silent signature — both documented in "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` (on `jusprin-newui` since 2026-09-13, commit `318208608f`).
- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. No `dxil.dll` → d3d12 initializes, then exit `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw with nothing logged. Both verified by removing the file and re-running. With all three present, both `d3d12` (default, `4.2 … D3D12`) and `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` (`4.6 … llvmpipe`) render.
- `slow_bootup` only moves the dxil crash from startup to first canvas paint; it is not a workaround.
- Lesson: a clear-only WGL smoke test passed under d3d12 because clearing compiles no shader, and was wrongly read as clearing the driver. A smoke test that skips the suspect code path proves nothing about it. (That test was removed from the repo for this reason.)
- A first-run datadir (e.g. copies of `C:\b\dd3`) logs ~630k lines in the first minute — the `GuideFrame::GetFilamentInfo` profile scan, driver-independent. Not a GL symptom.
- `D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` in the log is **Mesa's own d3d12 gallium driver on WARP**, not Microsoft's GLon12 mapping layer and not a real GPU. Confirm which GL is live by listing the process's loaded modules: the bundled Mesa shows `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (+ `DXIL.dll` once d3d12 has drawn), the unprovisioned fallback shows only `C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\OPENGL32.dll`.
- The permission guard has refused `Remove-Item` under `C:\b` in some sessions (reported as a protected path) and misparses `rd /s /q` and path-like string literals as delete targets. On 2026-10-23, in bypass-permissions mode with the user asking for the delete, `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` under `C:\b` worked. Build trees there contain a `src\Release\resources` junction into a worktree: list links first (`Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Attributes ReparsePoint`) and remove each with `[IO.Directory]::Delete(<link>)`, which deletes the link only, before any recursive delete.
- A debugger can be had without admin: download `https://aka.ms/windbg/download` (an .appinstaller pointing at a ~1.2 GB msixbundle), unzip the bundle, unzip `windbg_win-x64.msix`, and `amd64/cdb.exe` runs directly. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1` when running the harness under cdb, or teardown crawls in the debug heap for many minutes.
- Fixture directories for the harness's visual modes must be short paths (e.g. `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\wp\...`); a long scratchpad path makes the profile-bundle copy exceed MAX_PATH and the fixture slice never validates.
- The harness prints everything on stderr; the exit code must be read with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell (bash shows 127).
- DPI at 150%/200% needs the user to reconnect the RDP session at that scale. See [[jusprin-windows-parity-handoff]].

Node is installed twice: the older `C:\tools\node` (v24.20.0), which is **not on PATH**, and
`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64` (v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0), added to the **user
PATH** on 2026-09-16. Check `Get-Command npm.cmd` before installing anything; a fresh Bash
session may still need `export PATH="$PATH:/c/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64"`.

npm is not optional any more: since commit `5fc0efe2e3` the Agent and Home pages are built from
TypeScript and their `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` is generated, not committed.
Without npm, CMake **fails at configure time** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt`
`FATAL_ERROR`), so the first new source file you add breaks the build tree; and without the
bundles the app creates no Agent WebView at all, which shows up as `shell_agent_webview_created
FAIL` / "the Agent page did not complete its handshake" in the shell harness. Build them with
`npm ci && npm run build` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `HomeUI`.

The shell harness and the Agent page must come from the same commit: a harness exe built before
a page change hangs at `agent_reply_streams_to_completion` instead of failing.

To work on `jusprin-mcp` (the MCP stdio helper) you do **not** need an app build, and a worktree
can have its own build tree in about three minutes: configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF`
(skips the npm requirement above) plus
`-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`, then
`cmake --build <dir> --config Release --target jusprin-mcp -- -m`, which compiles only the six

description: "git commit hangs in Entire's prepare-commit-msg on Windows because Entire opens CONIN$ for a [Y/n] link prompt; GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 makes it non-interactive"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 673eb384-7139-489f-8ef7-aa76f6ab7efa
  modified: 2026-09-27T05:53:11.186Z
---

Root cause (diagnosed 2026-09-25, Entire CLI 0.11.0): when the committing session has file changes to link,
`entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` shows "Link this commit to session context? [Y/n]" and reads the
answer from `CONIN$`, not stdin. The agent's Git Bash has a hidden console, so the open succeeds and the read blocks forever.
`</dev/null` does not help. Commits with nothing to link skip the prompt, which is why it looked intermittent.
The log is buffered, so `.entire/logs/entire.log` shows nothing until the process exits.
Evidence: handle dump of the hung process showed a `\Device\ConDrv` handle with a blocked synchronous read.
Entire's own Pi integration prefixes agent bash commands with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` for this exact reason.
With `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` the same hook finished in ~0.3s and added the trailer, 3 of 3 runs; without it, 3 of 3 hung.

**Why:** It looks like a slow checkpoint condense, so it is easy to wait a long time for nothing.
A separate, real slowdown also exists: an `msbuild -m` build pins all 16 cores (processor queue ~64) and every
`entire` launch then takes 5-20s. That is slow, not hung; don't confuse the two.

**How to apply:** Fixed 2026-09-25: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is set as a user env var (HKCU\Environment), so Claude and Codex
shells inherit it after the app restarts (verified in Claude: 3/3 hook runs 0.3s with trailer). If a commit hangs again, first check
`echo $GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` in the agent shell. Restarting the Claude app: the tray has no Quit, so end all `claude` processes
from a helper launched via WMI (outside Claude's tree) and relaunch with `explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude`.
If one hangs anyway, kill only that commit's `entire` PID; never `--no-verify`. See [[windows-build-machine]].

2026-09-27: with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` already set, a `git merge --no-ff` (merge commit) in a worktree still ran past a
120 s `timeout` -- but the merge commit was already written correctly and nothing was left running. After a timeout, check
`git log -1` and the parents before retrying; a retry would make a second commit. A plain `git commit` minutes earlier took ~seconds.

Kenneth decided (2026-09-28) that prompt changes are evaluated on DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to hosts that answer the app's developer notes (`tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py` defaults), and on no other model. I had kept running and reporting the app's own gpt-5.4-mini next to it on every change; he asked why I treated the app's model as special, and had me remove the `--app` option and every "also check the app's model" instruction.

**Why:** it doubled cost and numbers to read, made the app's model look like a second judge, and JusPrin will soon support other providers, so today's default model isn't what users will necessarily get.

On 2026-10-13 Kenneth applied the same rule to the project assistant's journeys (`shell_integration_harness --journey`, `tests/project_journey/`): DeepSeek on OpenRouter with its hosted tool search, not the app's gpt-5.4-mini, even though the app's namespace deferral exists only on the OpenAI route. He put the keys on the Windows box that day at `C:\Users\guitest\.config\jusprin\prompt-test.env` (`export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=`, `export OPENAI_API_KEY=`); read them from there, never print them. He still approves the run count and token estimate before each live batch.

**How to apply:** judge and report prompt edits with the harness defaults only (paired `--prompt-rev HEAD` run). Use `--model` only when he asks to compare models. The real-app check (`shell_harness --printer-live`) still uses whatever the app is configured with; that's an app check, not a prompt evaluation. See [[fix-without-breaking-other-scenarios]].

1	# Project chat prompt tests
2	
3	The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
4	(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the project
5	tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
6	step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
7	sentence of the prompt. It is run against the prompt before an edit and after it, and the
8	counts compared. The app does not run.
9	
10	On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
11	`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
12	agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:
13	
14	```bash
15	( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
16	```
17	
18	Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
19	or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
20	runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
21	approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
22	exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.
23	
24	The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
25	"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
26	Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge. `--backend
27	claude-cli` runs the same cases on the developer's Claude subscription
28	instead, for iterating on a prompt without API cost (see "Running on the
29	Claude subscription").
30	
31	## One step, with its reads answered
32	
33	Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
34	step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
35	app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
36	order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:
37	
38	- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
39	  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
40	  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered.
41	- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
42	  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
43	  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
44	- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
45	  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
46	  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
47	  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
48	  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
49	  app's "not run" result instead.
50	- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
51	  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
52	  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.
53	
54	A call the app would refuse gets the app's refusal, as ProviderAgent gives
55	it: a tool not offered on the request is `unknown_tool`, and arguments that
56	`ToolRegistry::validate_call` does not accept get its own code and message
57	(`tests/agent/tool_call_check` runs that check, so the runner refuses exactly
58	what the app refuses, schema rules and the registry's own alike). Every
59	later call of that response is answered "not run", and the run goes on. A
60	refused call is never judged, read or change: the case sees only the calls
61	before it. The app answers two refused calls a turn and fails the turn on
62	the third (`malformed_tool_call`); so does a run. Before 2026-10-20 the
63	runner answered such reads from the recording, so earlier counts could pass
64	a call the app would have refused.
65	A run's report names every call of the response it ended on. `test_steps.py`
66	checks these rules offline against written model outputs, with no key and
67	nothing sent (`python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`).
68	
69	The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
70	`answers` list names:
71	
72	- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
73	  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`; `slice_report` of the

400	## Running it
401	
402	The runner and `test_steps.py` need the app's argument check built:
403	`cmake --build <build dir> --config <config> --target tool_call_check`. The
404	runner takes the newest one under `build/` (or `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`) and
405	stops when it is older than `ToolRegistry.cpp`.
406	
407	By default every case runs 3 times (`RUN_BUDGET` 60 shared by the cases run,
408	at most 20 for one case alone); `--runs N` sets it. `--verbose` prints every
409	run's conversation. Usage is logged for every response on stderr and totalled
410	at the end.
411	
412	```bash
413	tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only --prompt-rev 6b4b8b6188 > bodies.jsonl
414	```
415	
416	prints every request body it would send and their sizes, and sends nothing.
417	
418	All runs of all the cases run share one pool of `--jobs` workers (5 by
419	default, 3 for the claude-cli backend below), and each run's line gives its
420	wall-clock time.

422	## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)
423	
424	`--backend claude-cli` answers every step with the locally installed Claude
425	Code CLI in headless mode (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude
426	subscription instead of a per-token API key. `--judge claude-cli` moves the
427	judge there as well. Neither needs a key; both need the CLI logged in once
428	with `claude auth login`. The runner refuses to start a run the CLI would bill
429	to an API key (`apiKeySource` other than the login).
430	
431	```bash
432	tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --case advice-infill --runs 1
433	```
434	
435	The model defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` at effort `medium`, both pinned so a
436	count moves only when the prompt does (`--claude-model`, `--claude-effort`,
437	`--claude-judge-model`). `--claude-keep DIR` keeps each run's session file,
438	tool list, MCP config and the CLI's event stream for reading afterwards.
439	
440	### Which backend for what
441	
442	- **Iterating on a prompt or skill: the subscription.** A strong model
443	  answering the app's real requests, with real tool calls, shows what the
444	  prompt itself causes: an ambiguous sentence, a rule two sections disagree
445	  on, a skill that invites the wrong call. It costs no API money, so it can
446	  be run as often as the subscription's usage limits allow. Those limits are
447	  shared with the developer's own Claude Code work; start with one case and
448	  keep `--jobs` small.
449	- **Before a release: a small paid run on the app's default model.** The app
450	  defaults to `gpt-5.4-mini` (the OpenAI provider's default in
451	  `ProviderProfile.hpp`), which scored about like DeepSeek V4 Flash in the
452	  printer suite's model table (82 and 79 of 87, `tests/printer_prompt`,
453	  "Which model"). A strong model
454	  can paper over an ambiguity a weaker one trips on, so a pass on Opus does
455	  not show the shipped default will pass. That run needs Kenneth's approval
456	  like every paid batch.
457	- **The baselines below** are DeepSeek V4 Flash with the OpenAI judge, except
458	  the subscription baseline, which is claude-cli's own. A claude-cli count is
459	  compared only with that one. Changing the judge changes
460	  what every judged case counts, so `--judge claude-cli` results start their
461	  own baseline, under the same "confirmed results become the baseline" rule.
462	
463	### How a recorded request reaches the CLI
464	
465	`claude_cli.py` turns each recorded request into a CLI run, and
466	`claude_mcp_stub.py` serves the tools:
467	
468	- **System prompt**: the rendered prompt, as `--system-prompt`.
469	- **Tools**: the stub is a stdio MCP server with the case's tools (the 29 of
470	  `project_tools.json`, or the point's own list), with their real
471	  descriptions and schemas. Every call the model makes reaches the runner
472	  through it, and the step rules above apply unchanged: a read is answered
473	  with the recorded answer, a change ends the run (the runner stops the CLI;
474	  nothing is answered), a response of reads decides or is answered whole.
475	- **History**: the request's items before its last turn are written as a
476	  session file the CLI resumes (`--resume <file>`), so earlier messages,
477	  calls and results reach the model as its own turns, tool calls and tool
478	  results, not as a transcript. The last turn's message (the person's words,
479	  the `<workspace>` block, the plate's picture) goes in as one stream-json
480	  user message.
481	- **A point recorded mid-turn**, after a tool result (`after-preview`,
482	  `after-apply`, `after-slice`, `after-intent`, `direct-change-applied`,
483	  `direct-change-failed`, `first-person`, `slice-refused-by-tool`): the
484	  session ends on that turn's last call, marked as a deferred call. The CLI
485	  runs it through the stub, which returns the recorded result, and then asks
486	  the model.
487	
488	Nothing from the developer's own Claude Code setup reaches the model: no
489	CLAUDE.md, auto-memory, settings, hooks, output style, skills, other MCP
490	servers or built-in tools, a minimal environment, and an empty temporary
491	working directory. `test_claude_cli.py` checks that, and the shapes above,
492	by running the installed CLI against a fake Messages endpoint on localhost
493	(no login, nothing sent; about 10 seconds). Run it after a CLI update: the
494	session file is the CLI's internal format, verified against 2.1.283.
495	
496	What differs from the app's request, beyond the model:
497	
498	- **Developer messages.** The Messages API has no developer role, so each of
499	  the app's developer items (its notes after a file-load report, the skills)
500	  is a user text block wrapped in `<developer_message>` tags. Hosts that
501	  drop or demote the developer role raise the same question for the API
502	  backend.
503	- **The CLI's own text.** Before the prompt, the CLI sends a billing header
504	  and "You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK."; after
505	  the first message it adds a short environment note (the temporary working
506	  directory, platform, date and model name) and an empty system turn
507	  carrying the effort setting.
508	- **Tool names** carry the CLI's MCP prefix: the model sees
509	  `mcp__jusprin__settings_get`, while descriptions, which name other tools
510	  bare, are unchanged. The runner strips the prefix.
511	- **Mid-turn points**: after the deferred call's result, the CLI adds
512	  "Continue from where you left off." as a user message. The app's notes
513	  that follow the result there (the setup skill in `after-intent`, the
514	  slice-failed skill in `slice-refused-by-tool`) are further text blocks of
515	  that same tool result, since the CLI resumes no message after it.
516	- **Notes sent once** (a point's `once`) stay in the history after the
517	  first answered read; the app leaves them out of the turn's later requests.
518	- **Pictures** reach the model, unlike on the pinned DeepSeek hosts, so
519	  `model-opened-unnamed`, `model-imported-by-tool` and `model-opened-by-tool`
520	  can be measured here.
521	
522	The usage the runner logs is the CLI's token count; on the subscription it is
523	not billed per token.

525	## Judging a prompt or skill change
526	
527	What the suite is for (Kenneth, 2026-10-19): showing that a change has not
528	made the prompt substantially worse. At three runs a case it detects large
529	regressions only, not small effects. Day-to-day host noise is small next to
530	what it looks for: on the printer suite the same prompt scored 76, 76 and 74
531	of 84 on three runs.
532	
533	1. After a prompt or skill change, run the "after" batch only: the checkout,
534	   same model, pinned hosts and judge, three runs a case. Compare it with the
535	   current baseline table below. There is no before run.
536	2. Judging the result. There are no fixed thresholds (Kenneth,
537	   2026-10-19). The agent running the batch compares it with the baseline
538	   case by case and reads every failure and unobserved run. It decides
539	   whether anything looks like a real regression worth investigating, and
540	   says why. A case with no baseline row is judged on its own expectation.
541	   When it is not sure, it asks Kenneth.
542	3. Only for a case that looks like a regression, run it again with
543	   `--prompt-rev <previous revision>` the same day. That tells the prompt
544	   apart from changed requests or a bad host day; a bad host day usually shows
545	   as drops in untouched cases too. A case run alone gets 20 runs, which is
546	   what to use before reading a smaller gap as real.
547	4. Baselines. The current baseline is one section. When Kenneth confirms a
548	   new result is good enough, it becomes the new baseline, and the old one
549	   moves to "Baseline history" below, kept for audit only and not used for
550	   comparison.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""One step of the project chat against the live model, without the app.
3	
4	The project chat's assistant is a system prompt (projectInstructions.ts), the
5	project tools and the chat. Each case here is one point in a project chat,
6	recorded from the real app, and the model's next step there, a tool call or a
7	reply, checked against one sentence of the prompt. A response may hold
8	several calls, and every one is judged: a change among them is the outcome
9	and ends the run, whatever came before it. A response of reads the case does
10	not decide on is answered, each read with the result the app gave for it at
11	the same point (recorded beside the request), and the model asked again, at
12	most MAX_READS times; nothing else is ever answered.
13	
14	What the app sends, reproduced here:
15	  - instructions: rendered from projectInstructions.ts by
16	    tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs, so an edit to the prompt is tested
17	    without building anything;
18	  - tools: project_tools.json, the app's own tool list for the project chat
19	    (test_openai_responses_agent.cpp fails if it drifts from the registry);
20	  - input: everything else, as the app built it (requests.json). The shell
21	    harness's --project-prompt-requests mode plays script.json through the
22	    real app, with the model's outputs scripted and every tool run for real,
23	    and keeps the request at each point a case observes: the earlier turns as
24	    the app replays them, this turn's message with the workspace context, and
25	    this turn's calls with their live results. At the same point it calls
26	    the reads script.json's "answers" lists (workspace_inspect, slice_report,
27	    printer_list, object_analyze for each object, settings_get of every
28	    setting of the print, the first object, the filament and the printer,
29	    the filament's and printer's names asked under the print scope, a
30	    hand-kept list of other slicers' names, and settings_search for common
31	    queries) and keeps
32	    their results: those are the only answers a read can get.
33	The app streams its requests; this script does not. Nothing else differs,
34	except which model answers them.
35	
36	Usage:
37	  OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py
38	      [--runs N] [--must-pass N] [--case NAME] [--jobs 5] [--verbose] [--prompt-rev REV]
39	      [--model NAME [--endpoint URL] [--key-env NAME] [--provider HOST]...]
40	  tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli [--claude-model M] [--claude-effort E]
41	      [--judge claude-cli [--claude-judge-model M]] [--claude-keep DIR] [other flags as above]
42	  tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only [--case NAME] [--runs N] [--prompt-rev REV]
43	
44	--backend claude-cli answers each step with the local Claude Code CLI in
45	headless mode, on the developer's Claude subscription (claude_cli.py says
46	how a request reaches it); --judge claude-cli moves the judge there too. Both
47	need `claude auth login` done once; neither needs an API key.
48	
49	--render-only sends nothing: it prints each case's full request body, one JSON
50	object per line, and on stderr the size of each and of the batch.
51	
52	Prompt changes are evaluated on DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to
53	the hosts tests/printer_prompt names (MODEL, PROVIDERS), and on nothing else.
54	The judge stays on OpenAI (OPENAI_API_KEY) whichever model answers.
55	
56	Without --runs, the cases run share RUN_BUDGET runs: 3 each for 26 cases,
57	never more than MAX_RUNS for one case.
58	
59	Exit code 0 when every case passes at least --must-pass of its runs (default:
60	all of them), 1 otherwise. Needs python3 and node, and the page's npm install
61	(src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/node_modules) for esbuild.

124	class CallCheck:
125	    """The app's own check of a call's arguments: tests/agent/tool_call_check,
126	    ToolRegistry::validate_call as a command, so a call is refused exactly
127	    when the app refuses it and in its words. Found under build/ (the newest
128	    one), or named by JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK; built with
129	    `cmake --build <build dir> --target tool_call_check`."""
130	
131	    def __init__(self):
132	        self.process, self.lock = None, threading.Lock()
133	
134	    @staticmethod
135	    def path():
136	        if os.environ.get("JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK"):
137	            return pathlib.Path(os.environ["JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK"])
138	        root = HERE.parents[1]
139	        found = [path for pattern in ("build/*/tests/agent/*/", "build/*/tests/agent/", "build/tests/agent/*/",
140	                                      "build/tests/agent/")
141	                 for name in ("tool_call_check", "tool_call_check.exe") for path in root.glob(pattern + name)]
142	        if not found:
143	            raise RuntimeError("tool_call_check is not built: run `cmake --build <build dir> --target tool_call_check` "
144	                               "or set JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK")
145	        newest = max(found, key=lambda path: path.stat().st_mtime)
146	        registry = root / "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp"
147	        if registry.stat().st_mtime > newest.stat().st_mtime:
148	            raise RuntimeError(f"{newest} is older than ToolRegistry.cpp: rebuild the tool_call_check target")
149	        return newest

181	def post(body, key, endpoint=ENDPOINT):
182	    request = urllib.request.Request(endpoint, data=json.dumps(body).encode(), method="POST",
183	                                     headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + key, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
184	    for attempt in range(5):
185	        try:
186	            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120) as response:
187	                return json.load(response)
188	        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
189	            # 403 is a spent key: stop, never retry or switch keys.
190	            if error.code not in (429, 500, 502, 503) or attempt == 4:
191	                raise RuntimeError(f"HTTP {error.code}: {error.read().decode(errors='replace')[:500]}")
192	        except (urllib.error.URLError, ConnectionError):  # ConnectionError: a reset mid-response
193	            if attempt == 4:
194	                raise
195	        time.sleep(2 ** attempt)

227	def judge(log, question):
228	    """A yes or no about the conversation's last reply, from a stronger model,
229	    for what no string test can check. Returns (yes, why)."""
230	    schema = {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False, "required": ["answer", "why"],
231	              "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}, "why": {"type": "string"}}}
232	    instructions = ("You read a chat between a 3D printing app's assistant and a person, and answer one "
233	                    "question about it strictly as written, judging only what the messages say.")
234	    prompt = "\n".join(log) + "\n\nQuestion: " + question
235	    if CLAUDE_JUDGE:
236	        verdict, usage = claude_cli.judge(instructions, prompt, schema, *CLAUDE_JUDGE)
237	        count(usage, judge=True)
238	        return verdict["answer"] == "yes", verdict["why"]
239	    response = post({"model": JUDGE_MODEL, "store": False, "instructions": instructions, "input": prompt,
240	                     "text": {"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "verdict", "strict": True, "schema": schema}}},
241	                    os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], JUDGE_ENDPOINT)
242	    count(response.get("usage"), judge=True)
243	    text = "".join(output_text(item) for item in response.get("output", []) if item.get("type") == "message")
244	    verdict = json.loads(text)

273	class Step:
274	    """What the model did with the request: its reply, or the tool call that
275	    stands for its calls. A response may hold several calls, and the app runs
276	    every one, so a change among them is the step whatever came before it
277	    (the first change, if several); a response of reads is the first read,
278	    and each_read() gives a step for every read. Every call is in the report."""
279	
280	    def __init__(self, output, index=None):
281	        self.output = output
282	        self.calls = [item for item in output if item.get("type") == "function_call"]
283	        self.reply = "".join(output_text(item) for item in output if item.get("type") == "message").strip()
284	        if index is None:
285	            index = next((i for i, item in enumerate(self.calls) if item.get("name") not in READS), 0)
286	        self.index = index
287	        call = self.calls[index] if self.calls else None
288	        self.tool = call["name"] if call else None
289	        self.call_id = call.get("call_id") if call else None
290	        self.arguments = self.parsed(call) if call else {}
291	
292	    @staticmethod
293	    def parsed(call):
294	        try:
295	            return json.loads(call.get("arguments") or "{}")
296	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
297	            return {"(unreadable)": call.get("arguments")}
298	
299	    def each_read(self):
300	        """A step for every call of a response with no change in it, in the
301	        order the model wrote them."""
302	        return [Step(self.output, index) for index in range(len(self.calls))]
303	
304	    def before(self, index):
305	        """The response as far as the app runs it when its call at index is
306	        refused: the calls before it, and no reply, since the turn goes on."""
307	        kept, seen = [], 0
308	        for item in self.output:
309	            if item.get("type") == "function_call":
310	                if seen < index:
311	                    kept.append(item)
312	                seen += 1
313	        return Step(kept)
314	
315	    def keys(self):
316	        """The settings a settings call names."""
317	        return set(self.arguments.get("keys") or []) | set(self.arguments.get("changes") or {})
318	
319	    def changes(self):
320	        return self.tool is not None and self.tool not in READS
321	
322	    def reads(self):
323	        return self.tool in READS
324	
325	    def __str__(self):
326	        if not self.tool:
327	            return "reply: " + (self.reply.replace("\n", " ")[:160] or "(empty)")
328	        text = f"{self.tool} {json.dumps(self.arguments, ensure_ascii=False)}"
329	        others = [f"{call['name']} {json.dumps(self.parsed(call), ensure_ascii=False)}"
330	                  for index, call in enumerate(self.calls) if index != self.index]
331	        return text + (f" [same response: {'; '.join(others)}]" if others else "")

339	# is a read the case does not decide on: when it decides on none of a
340	# response's reads, the runner answers them all from the recording and asks
341	# again. UNOBSERVED is a step the case can say nothing about, or a read with

349	    def judged(self, step, question):
350	        yes, why = judge(self.log + ["assistant: " + step.reply], question)
351	        return yes, why

353	    def reply_or_read(self, step):
354	        """A reply passes, a change fails, a read is answered."""
355	        if step.changes():
356	            return FAIL, "CHANGED: " + str(step)
357	        return (CONTINUE if step.tool else PASS), str(step)

359	    def judged_reply(self, step, question, claim):
360	        """For cases about what a reply says: a change fails, a read is
361	        answered, and the reply fails when the judge says yes."""
362	        if step.tool:
363	            return (FAIL if step.changes() else CONTINUE), str(step)
364	        yes, why = self.judged(step, question)
365	        return (FAIL, claim + why) if yes else (PASS, str(step))

No. The brief only asks for one live run, after the change. For the baseline it gives a choice: seed it from the latest complete recorded results, "or record one live." It gives no reason to prefer the live recording, so I've paused before planning any live run.

So far I've only read the README and the runner, and moved this worktree's branch onto jusprin-newui (it had started from main). Nothing is edited and nothing has been sent to a model.

One thing to weigh before you choose. The latest complete DeepSeek results are from 2026-10-19, at dd9cf918af. Several things changed after that run:
- `intent_update` and `plan_set` were merged into `setup_record` (2026-10-20), which changed the tools and the recording.
- The two calibration cases were added on 2026-10-21, so they have no row.
- `after-filament-change` has since been removed.
- The three picture cases were never measured on the DeepSeek hosts.

So if the after-change run is compared with that seed, any difference could come from those earlier changes as well as from removing `fields`. A live baseline recorded first would separate the two, but it doubles the cost.

My suggestion is to seed from the 2026-10-19 results, mark the cases with no row, and only re-run a case on the old code if it moves a lot. That's what the README's own step 3 already says to do for a case that looks like a regression.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The runner's handling of the model's responses, offline: hand-written
outputs in place of the model, no key and no request sent. Above all a
response with several calls, which the runner once judged and answered by
its first call alone.

Usage: python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py
"""

import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import re
import unittest

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("run_prompt_tests", HERE / "run_prompt_tests.py")
runner = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(runner)


def call(name, arguments=None, call_id=None):
    return {"type": "function_call", "call_id": call_id or "call-" + name, "name": name,
            "arguments": json.dumps(arguments or {})}


def reply(text):
    return {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": text}]}


class Scripted:

def report(name, results, tally, must_pass, args):
    for index, (verdict, detail, log, seconds) in enumerate(results, 1):
        print(f"{name} run {index}/{args.runs}: {verdict} ({seconds:.0f} s): {detail}")
        if args.verbose or verdict != PASS:
            for line in log[-6:] if not args.verbose else log:
                print("    " + line.replace("\n", "\n    "))
    print(f"{name}: {tally[PASS]} of {args.runs} passed, {tally[FAIL]} failed, {tally[UNOBSERVED]} unobserved"
          + (f" (needs {must_pass})" if must_pass is not None else ""))


# --- Baseline ----------------------------------------------------------------
#
# A run is judged against a baseline kept in the repository, not against a
# second run of the old prompt. The baseline and a run's results are the
# same data: what answered (backend, model, hosts, judge), when and at which
# commit, the SHA-256 of the prompt, tool list and recording, and per case
# the runs, passes, fails and unobserved runs. Cases with no baseline are
# listed in noBaseline with the reason.

BASELINES = {"api": HERE / "baseline.json", "claude-cli": HERE / "baseline-claude-cli.json"}
# A case moves "a lot" when its share of passing runs moves by this much: at
# three runs, two runs or more (3 of 3 against 1 or 0 of 3). A move of one
# run is within what the same prompt does from day to day.
LARGE = 0.6
# The fields that must match for a run to be compared with a baseline; when
# one differs the baseline is re-recorded, not compared with.
SETUP = ("backend", "model", "effort", "hosts", "judge")


def sha256(data):
    import hashlib
    return hashlib.sha256(data.encode() if isinstance(data, str) else data).hexdigest()


def git(*args):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=HERE, capture_output=True, encoding="utf-8").stdout.strip()


def results_of(setup, instructions, tallies):
    """A run's results, in the baseline's form. tallies: {case: {runs, pass,
    fail, unobserved, errors}}, errors being failed runs that got no
    response (a host or network error). A case whose every run is an error
    measured nothing, so it goes to noBaseline."""
    cases = {name: tally for name, tally in tallies.items() if tally["errors"] < tally["runs"]}
    return {**setup, "date": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), "commit": git("rev-parse", "--short=10", "HEAD"),
            "uncommitted": bool(git("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no")),
            "sha256": {"prompt": sha256(instructions), "tools": sha256((HERE / "project_tools.json").read_bytes()),
                       "recording": sha256((HERE / "requests.json").read_bytes())},
            "cases": cases,
            "noBaseline": {name: "every run failed without a response" for name in tallies if name not in cases}}


def describe(data):
    hosts = f" on {', '.join(data['hosts'])}" if data.get("hosts") else ""
    effort = f" at effort {data['effort']}" if data.get("effort") else ""
    return f"{data['model']}{effort}{hosts} ({data['backend']}), judge {data['judge']}"


def compare(run, baseline):
    """Each case of the run beside the baseline, marking only the large moves.
    Returns (lines, worse): worse is the cases marked worse, or None when the
    run cannot be compared with this baseline at all."""
    lines = [f"Baseline: {baseline['date']} at {baseline['commit']}, {describe(baseline)}",
             f"This run: {run['date']} at {run['commit']}{' with uncommitted changes' if run.get('uncommitted') else ''}, "
             f"{describe(run)}"]
    differs = [field for field in SETUP if run.get(field) != baseline.get(field)]
    if differs:
        lines.append(f"NOT COMPARABLE: the {', '.join(differs)} differ from the baseline's. Compare only runs on the "
                     "baseline's setup; a new setup needs a baseline recorded on it (--record-baseline).")
        return lines, None
    changed = [what for what in ("tools", "recording")
               if run["sha256"][what] != (baseline.get("sha256") or {}).get(what)]
    if changed:
        lines.append(f"Note: the {' and the '.join({'tools': 'tool list', 'recording': 'recording'}[what] for what in changed)} "
                     "differ from the baseline's, so a moved case may come from that as well as from the prompt.")
    worse, better, noise = [], [], []
    lines.append(f"{'case':28} {'baseline':>16}   {'this run':>16}")
    def counts(tally):
        return f"{tally['pass']}/{tally['runs']} {tally['fail']}f {tally['unobserved']}u"
    for name, tally in run["cases"].items():
        base = baseline["cases"].get(name)
        if base is None:
            why = baseline.get("noBaseline", {}).get(name, "not in the baseline")
            lines.append(f"{name:28} {'-':>16}   {counts(tally):>16}   no baseline: {why}")
            continue
        moved = tally["pass"] / tally["runs"] - base["pass"] / base["runs"]
        mark = ""
        if moved <= -LARGE:
            worse.append(name)
            mark = "WORSE"
            # A drop made of runs that observed nothing, or got no response,
            # says more about the hosts or the recording than the prompt.
            failed_more = tally["fail"] / tally["runs"] - base["fail"] / base["runs"]
            errors = tally.get("errors", 0)
            if failed_more < LARGE or errors:
                noise.append(name)
                mark += " (may be noise: " + (f"{errors} request errors" if errors else "unobserved runs, not failures") + ")"
        elif moved >= LARGE:
            better.append(name)
            mark = "BETTER"
        lines.append(f"{name:28} {counts(base):>16}   {counts(tally):>16}   {mark}".rstrip())
    for name in run.get("noBaseline", {}):
        lines.append(f"{name:28} {'':>16}   {'no response':>16}   {run['noBaseline'][name]}")
    lines.append(f"{len(worse)} worse, {len(better)} better, {len(run['cases']) - len(worse) - len(better)} within noise "
                 f"(a move of less than {LARGE:.0%} of the runs).")
    if len(worse) >= 3:
        lines.append("Several cases dropped at once. A bad host day shows as drops in cases the change did not touch: "
                     "before reading a drop as the change, run that case alone on the previous revision "
                     "(--case NAME --prompt-rev REV) the same day.")
    elif worse:
        lines.append("Read every failed and unobserved run of a worse case; to tell the change from the hosts, run it "
                     "alone on the previous revision (--case NAME --prompt-rev REV) the same day.")
    return lines, worse


def record_baseline(path, results):
    missing = sorted(set(CASES) - set(results["cases"]) - set(results.get("noBaseline", {})))
    if missing:
        sys.exit(f"a baseline is recorded from a run of every case; this run has no {', '.join(missing)}")
    if results.get("promptRev"):
        sys.exit("a baseline is recorded from the checkout's prompt, not --prompt-rev")
    path.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"recorded {path.name}: {len(results['cases'])} cases, at {results['commit']}"
          + (" with uncommitted changes" if results.get("uncommitted") else ""))

def finish(run, baseline_path, must_pass):
    """Prints the run beside the baseline. False when a case is marked worse,
    or, with no baseline to compare with and no --must-pass, always true."""
    if not baseline_path.exists():
        print(f"no baseline at {baseline_path.name}: nothing to compare with")
        return True
    lines, worse = compare(run, json.loads(baseline_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    print("\n" + "\n".join(lines))
    # With --must-pass the pass counts decide, as before baselines.
    return must_pass is not None or not worse

1. After a prompt or skill change, run the "after" batch only: the checkout,
   same model, pinned hosts and judge, three runs a case. Compare it with the
   current baseline table below. There is no before run.
2. Judging the result. There are no fixed thresholds (Kenneth,
   2026-10-19). The agent running the batch compares it with the baseline
   case by case and reads every failure and unobserved run. It decides
   whether anything looks like a real regression worth investigating, and
   says why. A case with no baseline row is judged on its own expectation.
   When it is not sure, it asks Kenneth.
3. Only for a case that looks like a regression, run it again with
   `--prompt-rev <previous revision>` the same day. That tells the prompt
   apart from changed requests or a bad host day; a bad host day usually shows
   as drops in untouched cases too. A case run alone gets 20 runs, which is
   what to use before reading a smaller gap as real.
4. Baselines. The current baseline is one section. When Kenneth confirms a
   new result is good enough, it becomes the new baseline, and the old one
   moves to "Baseline history" below, kept for audit only and not used for
   comparison.
input.new_string:
1. After a prompt, skill, tool or recording change, run the new version
   only: the checkout, the default model, pinned hosts and judge, three runs
   a case (the runner's defaults, no flags). There is no before run. The
   runner ends by printing every case beside the stored baseline:

   ```
   case                             baseline           this run
   after-apply                     2/3 1f 0u          3/3 0f 0u
   first-person                    1/3 2f 0u          3/3 0f 0u   BETTER
   issue-explain                   2/3 0f 1u          0/3 0f 3u   WORSE (may be noise: unobserved runs, not failures)
   ```

   (passes of runs, fails, unobserved). It marks only a large move: a case's
   share of passing runs moving by 60% of the runs or more, which at three
   runs means two runs or more (3 of 3 against 1 or 0 of 3). A move of one
   run is what the same prompt does from day to day and is not marked.
2. Judging the result. There are no fixed thresholds beyond that mark
   (Kenneth, 2026-10-19). The agent running the batch reads every failure
   and unobserved run of every case, marked or not, decides whether anything
   looks like a real regression worth investigating, and says why. A case
   with no baseline (the comparison says why) is judged on its own
   expectation. When it is not sure, it asks Kenneth.
3. Host noise. The comparison flags a mark that may be the hosts rather than
   the change: a drop made of unobserved runs rather than failures (the model
   read something the recording does not hold), a drop with request errors,
   and three or more cases dropping at once (a bad host day shows as drops in
   cases the change did not touch). It also says when the tool list or the
   recording differ from the baseline's, so a move may come from them. Only
   for a case that looks like a regression, run it again alone on the
   previous revision, `--case NAME --prompt-rev <revision>`, the same day; a
   case run alone gets 20 runs, which is what to use before reading a smaller
   gap as real. `--prompt-rev` changes only the prompt: the tools and the
   recording stay the checkout's.
4. Re-recording the baseline. The baseline is `baseline.json` (DeepSeek V4
   Flash on the pinned hosts, the OpenAI judge) and, for the subscription,
   `baseline-claude-cli.json` (Opus 5.5 for model and judge). Each holds the
   model, hosts, judge, date and commit it was recorded at, the SHA-256 of
   its prompt, tool list and recording, and per case the runs, passes, fails
   and unobserved runs; `noBaseline` names the cases it has no counts for
   and why. Record a new one, with `--record-baseline` on a full run of every
   case (or `--compare FILE --record-baseline` on a saved one), when:
   - Kenneth accepts a deliberate change whose result differs from the
     baseline (a case added, removed or rewritten, a prompt or tool change
     whose new counts he confirms as good enough); or
   - the model, the hosts or the judge change. The runner refuses to compare
     a run on another setup than the baseline's and says so.
   The recorded file is committed with the change it measures. The old
   counts stay in git history; describe the new baseline in the README's
   "Current baseline" section and move the old description to "Baseline
   history".

## 2.3 Print intent

This surface answers: **What outcome does the user want?**

Instead of beginning with hundreds of process parameters, the product should ask for meaningful requirements.

### What should remain

- Intended use
- Visual versus functional priority
- Strength direction
- Accuracy requirements
- Important dimensions or clearances
- Heat, chemical, outdoor, food-contact, or flexibility requirements
- Desired surface quality
- Maximum acceptable print time
- Material or color requirements
- Acceptable and unacceptable support contact
- Whether this is a prototype or final part

### Why the agent cannot decide this alone

The same model can legitimately be printed with different orientations, materials, wall structures, infill, supports, and tolerances depending on its purpose.

A decorative prototype and a load-bearing final component may use identical geometry but require completely different plans.

### What the agent should do

Translate intent into technical settings. For example:

> “This is a visible decorative object, so I oriented it to protect the front surface, moved the seam to the rear, and accepted a longer print to reduce visible layer artifacts.”

The user should judge that reasoning without having to configure every underlying value.

The full intent editor should appear during project creation, import, or when requirements are incomplete. Afterward, Prepare should retain only a compact editable summary. Specialized questions such as food contact, flexibility, critical clearances, and protected support surfaces should appear contextually rather than in every project.

Some product state is not held anywhere in OrcaSlicer: the print intent, the pinned agent plan, semantic region annotations, physical facts the user confirmed about a printer, and the monitoring rules the user sets for automatic pausing. For this state, the "current Orca owner" step in the route above is a JusPrin store instead. Every other step stays the same. The rules are:

- **Storage.** State that belongs to a project (intent, plan, regions, conversation, and attachments) lives in the local project store, under a project ID that does not change. The current `ProjectStateDocument` is saved separately from model checkpoints. An imported project may contain the older `Auxiliaries/JusPrin/state.json`. It is read only to migrate it. In that document:
  - each chat owns its print intent, `printIntent`, and its plan, `plan` (with the setup title and the purpose setup beside them). The project's current intent and plan are the active chat's, read through `activeConversationId` and stored nowhere else; a new chat starts with a copy of the active chat's intent and no plan. An intent write inserts or updates one field by name, and each field carries its provenance; a plan write replaces the whole plan;
  - the region annotations, `regions`, describe the model in the workspace. A write replaces the whole list, and each record is stamped with a seq when it changes. Every saved model version records the list it was saved with, and restoring or resuming that version puts its list back.

  State that belongs to a printer (confirmed facts, monitoring policy) stays in app data, stored per printer identity, the way `PrinterFactsStore` keeps it. Confirmed facts carry an expiry, because the physical world changes without telling the app. See [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md).
- **Revision.** Every write has to signal that it happened, so that readers read again. Two questions are still **open**: which signal to use, and whether the signal invalidates actions that are already queued. They belong to the milestone that adds the first writer. The obvious answer would be to publish a `WorkspaceChangeReasons` bit and add that bit to `kInvalidatingReasons`. That cannot be built as described. `settings_apply_patch` requires its caller's `expectedRevision` to equal the current revision exactly. So if the revision goes up at any point between a client's preview and its apply, the apply fails as `stale_workspace`. An agent that recorded its plan between previewing and applying would make its own call fail. There is an existing example of the alternative: the edit feed (`WorkspaceEditHub`) reports a change without raising the revision. Decide separately for each kind of state. A region annotation generates OrcaSlicer artifacts, so it is a real change to the project. An answer about intent, or a statement of the plan, is not. In the code as built, writing a region record signals nothing by itself. The artifacts it generates are ordinary OrcaSlicer edits, and they raise the revision in the usual way. So an action that was queued before an annotation goes stale, exactly as it would after any other edit to the model.
- **Undo.** None of this state is in OrcaSlicer's undo stack. Results say `projectUndo: false`. Region annotations are the awkward case. They generate OrcaSlicer artifacts (modifier volumes, enforcers, blockers, paint), and those artifacts *are* in the undo stack. So project Undo can leave an annotation without its artifacts, or leave an artifact without its annotation. The `regions` section of `object_analyze` reports both situations, and `region_annotate` generates the artifacts again. The result of a place, divide, or repair lists the regions whose link to the geometry that operation broke.
- **Provenance (where a value came from).** Any field that records a fact about the world or about what the user wants also records its source: `file` (read from the project or a profile), `observed` (reported by a sensor or the printer, with a timestamp), `agent_inferred`, or `user_confirmed`. A tool marks a value `user_confirmed` only when the call is based on something the user explicitly said. Values the agent inferred stay `agent_inferred`. When a tool reads printer state, it reports the `configured` value and the `observed` value of the same fact separately, and it computes the `mismatches` between them itself. That comparison is not left to the model.
